newsitem.title: USA: Unicom natgas venture seeks 10-15 pct market share.
newsitem.headline: Unicom natgas venture seeks 10-15 pct market share.

text.p: Unicom Gas Services, a joint venture between Unicom Energy Services and Sonat Marketing Co, on Wednesday said it was aiming to capture 10 to 15 percent of the $6.0 billion Midwest commercial and industrial natural gas market in three to five years.
That market constitutes 8.0 billion cubic feet of natural gas a day, said Robert Gilpin, who heads the venture.
While initially estimating the size of the market at $6 billion annually, Gilpin later offered the figure of $6 billion to $8 billion, depending on pricing.

The agreement comes as Unicom Corp 's Chicago-based Commonwealth Edison electric utility braces to defend its service territory under deregulation. The commercial and industrial natural gas market is already deregulated.

"Right now, Commonwealth Edison serves customers that have no choice," William Downey, president of Unicom Energy Services, a unit of Unicom Corp, said in a news conference in Chicago. "If they have a choice, on what basis will they select Unicom? We're putting in place those key building blocks that we think will define why we are the preeminent supplier" by allowing customers to receive multiple services from Unicom.

As deregulation eventually allows residential customers to also choose among many providers for utility service, Unicom could either serve those customers through the new venture with Sonat or through another venture, Downey said.
The companies are committed to the Unicom Gas Services venture for at least three years, the companies said.
The upfront financial committment for the venture is not significant, as it will use Sonat's existing pipelines and Unicom's marketing resources, Downey said. Sonat Marketing is a unit of Sonat Inc
Unicom had considered other options for entering the commercial and industrial natural gas market, Downey said.
"We looked very hard at all the options and quite frankly, we thought this was an efficient and expedient way to get into this market for our customers," Downey said.
Unicom shares ended 3/8 higher at 23-1/8 Wednesday, and Sonat shares dropped 3/8 to 49-1/2.
